scenarios.title: Desert convoy ambush
scenarios.brief: An IED has hit your patrol and the enemy is still firing from a ridgeline. A conscious soldier 15 metres away is screaming, bright red blood soaking his left trouser leg.

steps.label: Return fire and take cover
steps.why: Care Under Fire starts with the threat, because nothing you do for the casualty survives unsuppressed fire.

steps.label: Direct him to apply his own tourniquet
steps.why: He is conscious and carrying a kit, so self-aid stops the bleeding without exposing a second person.

steps.label: Apply a hasty tourniquet high and tight
steps.why: If he cannot do it himself, a tourniquet over the clothing at the top of the limb stops the bleeding inside a minute.

steps.label: Move him to cover behind the vehicle
steps.why: Once the bleeding is stopped, getting him out of the beaten zone is the next priority.

distractors.label: Run a full blood sweep where he lies
distractors.why: A full sweep belongs in Tactical Field Care; under fire it keeps you both exposed for minutes.

distractors.label: Open the airway and check breathing
distractors.why: He is screaming, so the airway is open, and airway work is deferred until the scene is safer.

distractors.label: Fill in the casualty card
distractors.why: Documentation follows bleeding control and movement to cover, not the other way round.

scenarios.title: Industrial plant fire
scenarios.brief: An explosion at a chemical plant has left fire, heavy smoke and the risk of a second blast. A worker lies 10 metres from the flames, unconscious, right arm amputated below the elbow, blood pooling fast.

steps.label: Assess the fire, smoke and blast risk
steps.why: The scene is not safe, and a casualty is not worth two casualties.

steps.label: Plan the route and the drag to cover
steps.why: An unconscious casualty cannot help you, so decide how you will move him before you commit.

steps.label: Apply a hasty tourniquet high and tight on the stump
steps.why: A traumatic amputation always takes a tourniquet, and the bleeding has to stop inside a minute.

steps.label: Drag him clear of the flames
steps.why: With the bleeding controlled, the remaining threat to his life is the fire itself.

steps.label: Call for help and hand over what you did
steps.why: The responders arriving need the mechanism, the tourniquet and its time before they touch him.

distractors.label: Pack the stump with a hemostatic dressing
distractors.why: Packing is for wounds no tourniquet can reach; on a limb amputation the tourniquet is faster and surer.

distractors.label: Wrap him against heat loss
distractors.why: Hypothermia prevention is a Tactical Field Care task, done once he is out of the hazard.

distractors.label: Roll him into the recovery position where he lies
distractors.why: Positioning him beside the flames leaves you both in the blast radius; move him first.

scenarios.title: Post-contact patrol
scenarios.brief: Contact has ended and your patrol is in a secured alley. A soldier with a hasty tourniquet on his right thigh is now confused, pale and sweating, breathing 24 times a minute, with an armpit wound still bleeding.

steps.label: Reassess the thigh tourniquet and tighten or add a second
steps.why: It went on under fire over the uniform, so confirm it has stopped the bleeding before anything else.

steps.label: Pack the armpit wound and hold pressure for 3 minutes
steps.why: No tourniquet seats in the armpit, so hemostatic packing under firm pressure is the control.

steps.label: Confirm the airway while he is still talking
steps.why: Speech proves the airway is open now, and his falling mental status means you keep checking.

steps.label: Expose and roll him to check the chest and back
steps.why: Breathing at 24 a minute with torso trauma means looking for a penetrating chest wound, front and back.

steps.label: Check the radial pulse and treat for shock
steps.why: Pale, sweaty, confused and breathing fast is hemorrhagic shock until bleeding control proves otherwise.

steps.label: Get him off the ground and cover him
steps.why: He has lost enough blood to cool fast, whatever the weather is doing.

steps.label: Record the findings and times on the casualty card
steps.why: The tourniquet times and your findings are what the next level cannot reconstruct later.

distractors.label: Pack the chest wound with hemostatic gauze
distractors.why: Chest wounds are sealed, never packed, because gauze cannot reach bleeding inside the chest.

distractors.label: Loosen the thigh tourniquet to check the bleeding
distractors.why: Releasing a tourniquet on a casualty already in shock restarts the bleeding you stopped.

distractors.label: Splint the leg below the tourniquet
distractors.why: Splinting comes after MARCH is complete; it is not what is killing him.

scenarios.title: Vehicle rollover
scenarios.brief: A vehicle rolled over on a training exercise, with no enemy and the scene secured by others. A soldier lies unconscious, breathing with loud snoring, no visible bleeding, and the neck may have been hyperextended.

steps.label: Run a full blood sweep for hidden bleeding
steps.why: No visible blood is not the same as no bleeding; the sweep is how you rule it out.

steps.label: Open the airway with a jaw-thrust
steps.why: Snoring is a partial obstruction, and the rollover mechanism rules out tilting the head.

steps.label: Look, listen and feel for breathing
steps.why: Confirm the opened airway is actually moving air before you move on.

steps.label: Check the radial pulse and the skin for shock
steps.why: A present, strong radial pulse and warm skin let you call circulation stable for now.

steps.label: Insulate her from the ground and cover her
steps.why: An unconscious casualty on the ground loses heat steadily and cannot tell you about it.

steps.label: Record the head injury signs and report them
steps.why: Mechanism and time unconscious are details only you can give the receiving medics.

distractors.label: Open the airway with a head-tilt/chin-lift
distractors.why: The rollover may have injured the neck, so the head stays still and the jaw comes forward instead.

distractors.label: Sweep the mouth with a blind finger
distractors.why: A blind sweep drives debris deeper; only what you can see comes out.

distractors.label: Roll her into the recovery position
distractors.why: A suspected spinal injury stays flat with the jaw held forward rather than being rolled onto her side.

scenarios.title: Building collapse
scenarios.brief: An IED has brought down part of a building and the threat is neutralised. A conscious, anxious soldier has a deep groin laceration bleeding heavily and an obviously deformed left forearm.

steps.label: Pack the groin wound with a hemostatic dressing
steps.why: No tourniquet reaches the groin, so packing onto the bleeding source is the control.

steps.label: Hold firm direct pressure for 3 full minutes
steps.why: The dressing only works if the clot is given the full three minutes to form.

steps.label: Apply a pressure bandage over the packing
steps.why: The bandage holds the packing in place so you can free your hands for the rest of MARCH.

steps.label: Roll him and check the torso front and back
steps.why: A blast casualty gets a chest check even when he is talking comfortably.

steps.label: Watch the radial pulse and skin for shock
steps.why: He has lost a lot of blood from the groin, so shock is the thing you expect next.

steps.label: Replace blood-soaked clothing and cover him
steps.why: Soaked clothing cools him faster than the bare air would.

steps.label: Splint the forearm and recheck the fingers
steps.why: Splinting follows MARCH, taking in the elbow and the wrist, with circulation checked before and after.

distractors.label: Apply a tourniquet to the groin
distractors.why: No limb tourniquet seats at the groin, and the attempt costs the minutes the packing needs.

distractors.label: Splint the forearm before anything else
distractors.why: The deformed forearm is obvious but not lethal; the groin bleed is what kills him.

distractors.label: Lift the packing after a minute to look
distractors.why: Lifting the dressing breaks the clot you are forming, so the three minutes start again.

scenarios.title: Training range blast
scenarios.brief: An accidental explosion on a training range, threat secured, bystanders on hand to help. A conscious soldier has blistered burns on both forearms, debris in his right eye and a swollen, deformed right ankle.

steps.label: Run a blood sweep to rule out massive bleeding
steps.why: Visible injuries pull the eye, so the sweep is what proves nothing is bleeding out.

steps.label: Confirm the airway and let him sit up
steps.why: He is talking, so the airway is open, and sitting up is the position he breathes best in.

steps.label: Check for respiratory distress and chest wounds
steps.why: A blast can injure the lungs even where the skin is unmarked.

steps.label: Check the radial pulse and watch for shock
steps.why: Burns and a fracture both bleed into tissue, so circulation is monitored rather than assumed.

steps.label: Cover the burns with dry dressings and insulate him
steps.why: Burned skin cannot hold heat, so the burn dressing and hypothermia prevention are one move.

steps.label: Shield the injured eye and tape the shield in place
steps.why: A rigid shield over that eye alone protects the globe without any pressure on it.

steps.label: Splint the ankle and recheck pulse and sensation
steps.why: The splint takes in the knee and the foot, with circulation checked before and after.

distractors.label: Lay wet dressings on the burns
distractors.why: Wet dressings pull heat out of a casualty already at risk of hypothermia.

distractors.label: Pick the debris out of the eye
distractors.why: Removing debris can empty the globe; the eye is shielded and the object left alone.

distractors.label: Bandage both eyes together
distractors.why: Only the injured eye is shielded, because blinding him costs him the ability to help himself.
